inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: A ceasefire that treats this as a deal between equals risks disguising the power imbalance and letting the causes of the conflict go unaddressed. Israel’s claim to pre-emptive force cannot simply be accepted while Iran is expected to settle for terms that leave aggression, accountability, and sovereignty unresolved. The people who bear the costs of war need more than leaders declaring a deal: any agreement must constrain the use of force, protect people, and confront the conditions that keep the conflict going.
